content.comment_body: I set up [product_name] and [product_name] Web Editor successfully; locally, when I access the [product_name] IP address, the web page loads as expected. For the past few months, connecting from outside via my router's IP with the port open results in strange behavior. My question is: why does the [product_name] Web Editor page fail to open on an iPhone when accessed remotely, while it works fine on a Samsung mobile? With the iPhone it's not possible. I mistakenly joined this conversation and can't start a new discussion, so I am requesting help from moderators.

Hello [user_name], Please post your question in English. This forum is international and using English increases the chance of helpful responses. Here is the translation of your post (from Google Translate): Kind regards, [user_name]

I configured [product_name] and [product_name] Web Editor correctly; locally, entering the [product_name] IP address opens the web page. When connecting externally via my local router's IP and with the port open, I encounter issues. Specifically, when accessing with an iPhone, the [product_name] Web Editor page does not load, whereas it works correctly with a Samsung phone. It seems impossible with iPhone.
Is there anyone who can help solve my issue? I need to connect to [product_name] version [version_no] using [product_name] Web Editor to check variable statuses over the internet.
Hi, Some suggestions: 1. Disconnect all other devices connected to the [product_name] Web Server. 2. Clear all browser data on your iPhone and try connecting again. Hope this is useful.

Hello, in my earlier post I noted that pages created with [product_name] Web Editor, which query [product_name] version [version_no] from the local network, work fine. However, from the internet, Android phones access these pages without issues, but iPhones cannot reach the same pages. The problem arises when the password prompt appears, showing error 601. I believe this is a communication protocol issue. Hopefully, this clarifies the problem, which remains unresolved.

Has anyone else encountered problems connecting with an iPhone through a router's external port to a page made with [product_name] Web Editor and received error 601 after entering the password? How can I report this to [company_name]? Everything works normally with Android; the issue is only with iPhone. If needed, I can share my router IP in private for troubleshooting.

Hi, iPhone should work. Try clearing your web browser cache on the device. Please note, only one device can be used with the web server at a time. If you enabled "Keep me logged in" on the login page, other devices may not be able to connect to the web page.

I've tried everything, but still can't connect to [product_name] version [version_no] using an iPhone. With other phones, entering my local server's IP and adding ":8090" (the open port for external access) connects quickly. If you want, I can provide the link privately; any support would be appreciated since I've been troubleshooting this for two months without success.

Hello [user_name], I am writing to you because I'm experienced with [product_name] version [version_no] issues, but not with how this forum operates, especially regarding solving programming challenges. My issue is: '[I configured [product_name] and [product_name] Web Editor correctly; locally, entering the [product_name] IP opens the page. For months, when accessing externally via my router's IP, I encounter strange issues—specifically, the Web Editor page does not open on iPhone but does on Samsung phones.]' I also noted: 'Previously, I mentioned that with Android you can reach the pages, but with iPhone it is impossible; error 601 appears at the password prompt. I suspect a protocol problem.' I've been unable to connect with my iPhone SE to [product_name] version [version_no] Web Editor remotely for three months, though Samsung devices work. Can [user_name] help?
[user_name] cannot answer? Can they contact technical support?

analysis.insight_summary: The main challenge is remote access to the [product_name] Web Editor page on an iPhone, which fails at the login step with error 601. Android devices work seamlessly with the same setup. Users believe the issue may be due to communication protocol or session management differences and express frustration at not finding a solution or receiving adequate support.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable, remote access to [product_name] Web Editor from any mobile device, including iPhone, and seek a solution to the error 601 encountered during login.
